scope: Second option matrix batch; only source-checklist-complete options may close.

source:
C: option.c:609–610; forward.c:268–320, 391–395, 1292, 1323–1340,
1457–1518, 3232–3276; rfc1035.c:extract_name. Rust consumers exist in
config/dns.rs and dns/forward.rs. No runtime gap identified in this source read.

checklist.boundary: Compare absent/do/no/both flags in each order, repeat flags, and rejected unexpected arguments; compare syntax and actual startup diagnostic streams.

For UDP, record raw outbound question casing. `do && !no` randomizes only the first 32 alphabetic characters; digit, hyphen and label separator positions do not consume bits. Check short and more-than-64-letter mixed-case names.

Do not compare random bit patterns or random IDs exactly. Require C and Rust to obey the same enabled/disabled rules and collect 64 independent requests so a disabled RNG path cannot pass an enabled profile.

Reply with exact echoed question; then with exactly one alphabetic case bit flipped. Enabled UDP must reject the second response and accept a later correctly cased one. Disabled UDP follows C's case-insensitive lookup.

Compare exact client question bytes, including original mixed case. Coalesce two clients whose letter-case difference occurs after letter 32 and after letter 64; both receive their own original question case and ID.
Exercise TCP separately; its forwarding path does not use the UDP frec encoding step. Record the observed C behavior rather than imposing UDP rules.
Controls: force no outbound case changes in enabled mode; mutate restored client case; accept an incorrect-case response; delete an observation.

source:
C: option.c:5453–5462 (zero rejected); dnsmasq.c:1901–1915, 1994–2008,
1631–1650 (slot requires both child exit and pipe EOF). Rust's shared owner
already consumes max_tcp_connections. Reuse the schedule from
`dns_tcp_capacity_diff.py`; execute both daemons in the exact image with `-k`.

checklist.boundary: Syntax/startup: one, two and zero; zero must fail rather than become an unlimited or disabled TCP service. Retain invalid-number diagnostics.

Fill all slots with idle clients, then connect/send an additional client. The extra request waits in the kernel accept queue and receives no response until a slot is released; it is not reset or rejected prematurely.
Close one client and observe queued-client admission and reply. Repeat through both listener addresses so the limit is global rather than per socket.
Keep UDP queries successful during TCP saturation, repeat fill/drain, and check child/socket/PID cleanup on shutdown. Use UDP readiness so readiness itself does not temporarily consume a TCP slot.
Controls: serve the excess client early, drop its eventual response, report per-listener capacity, retain a child after shutdown.

source:
C: option.c:3485–3492 and 6309–6321; network.c:271; forward.c:1685–1725,
2416–2450. Rust config finalization and ingress policy consumers already exist.

checklist.boundary: Syntax/startup: absent, no argument, `net`, `host`, invalid value. Preserve exact diagnostic streams; Rust's static `bad local-service` differs from C's generic `error` and must remain visible until corrected.

With no explicit interface/listen-address ACL, `net` admits only directly connected source subnets. Test local and routed non-local IPv4/IPv6 clients, each through UDP and TCP, using veths inside this family's private namespace.
`host` creates loopback-only binding equivalent to C's interface=lo plus bind-interfaces; check both address families and non-loopback destination.
Explicit interface, except-interface or listen-address configuration disables local-service restrictions; cover each override independently.

Check source subnet boundaries and distinguish source admission from destination listener presence. Namespace route setup and interface deletion must be recorded and cleaned up without touching the host network.
Controls: invert one admission decision, retain local-service despite an explicit ACL, delete one IPv6 or TCP observation.
ARG_ONE rejects same-origin duplicate but permits CLI plus config; net wins over host across origins (option.c2032-2043/6316).

source:
C: option.c:3552–3575; forward.c:472–489, 628–670, 3204;
dnsmasq.c:1103. Rust ScalarConfig/FastRetry and ForwardTable retry deadlines are
connected. Reuse the stimuli from `dns_retry_failure_diff.py`, not its native C
execution wrapper.

checklist.boundary: Syntax/startup: absent, bare flag, `50`, `50,0`, `50,999`, `50,1000`, `50,1999`; reject `49`, nonnumeric fields and extra fields. Check exact output.

Blackhole one upstream: first send then exponential retry intervals; timeout milliseconds truncate to seconds. Compare C-derived event counts and ordering; retain actual timestamps and use explicit bounded scheduler jitter.
A successful reply cancels further retries; timeout stops retries. A subsecond timeout performs no timer retries after truncation to zero.

Retry send failure does not leak a forward slot; recovered transport can answer later queries. Observe upstream selection under strict order and the normal selection mode, with the same source-derived fixture for each side.
DNS local UDP/TCP queries remain responsive while a retry is pending.
Controls: suppress a retry, leave retries active after success, mutate the interval sequence, omit a deadline observation.
